summary: Builds a controllable NURBS skin between profile curves, curves on surfaces, holes, branches, or tube intersections with tangent and curvature control.

key_params.name: group
key_params.note: Profile group or face pattern to bridge; required for profile curves

key_params.name: bridge
key_params.note: Bridge all primitives, groups of N primitives, or skip every Nth primitive

key_params.name: inc
key_params.note: Pattern count for grouped/skipped bridge operations

key_params.name: order
key_params.note: Spline order for profile extraction and skinning

key_params.name: isodivs
key_params.note: Number of cross sections in the bridged surface

key_params.name: frenet
key_params.note: Normal orientation method for generated cross sections

key_params.name: csharp
key_params.note: Close cracks by making bridge ends sharp

common_gotchas: Always specify curves on surface when bridging surface profiles, or Bridge may use free-floating curves instead.
Higher precision creates dense surfaces with more knots; order 4 cubic curves are the optimized sweet spot.
Bridging trimmed surfaces is more expensive than bridging carved surfaces.
Sharp-end crack fixing can add knots that create ripples in the bridged surface.
key_concepts: Bridge SOP builds NURBS skins between profile curves, faces, holes, branches, or tube intersections.
Profiles may come from curves on surfaces, and grouping determines which curves or faces are paired.
Bridge precision, order, tangent, and curvature controls trade surface quality against density and cook cost.
Trimmed-surface bridging is more expensive than carved-surface bridging and can need extra cleanup.
